The '''2008–09 Serie A''' (known as the [[Serie A]] [[Telecom Italia Mobile|TIM]] for sponsorship reasons) was the 107th season of top-tier Italian [[association football|football]], the 77th in a [[round-robin tournament]]. It began on 30 August 2008 and ended on 31 May 2009, with the announcement of the list of fixtures made on 25 July 2008. 20 teams competed in the league, 17 of which returned from [[2007–08 Serie A|the previous season]], and three ([[A.C. ChievoVerona|Chievo]], [[Bologna F.C. 1909|Bologna]] and [[U.S. Lecce|Lecce]]) were promoted from [[2007–08 Serie B]].

20 clubs represented 13 different [[Regions of Italy|regions]]. The most represented region was [[Lombardy]] with three teams: [[Atalanta B.C.|Atalanta]], [[A.C. Milan]], and [[Inter Milan]]. [[Piedmont]], [[Liguria]], [[Tuscany]], [[Lazio]] and [[Sicily]] featured two teams each while [[Friuli-Venezia Giulia]], [[Veneto]], [[Emilia-Romagna]], [[Campania]], [[Apulia]], [[Calabria]], and [[Sardinia]] were represented by one team each. There was a record number of southern teams in the top division with six teams: [[Cagliari Calcio|Cagliari]], [[Calcio Catania|Catania]], [[U.S. Lecce|Lecce]], [[S.S.C. Napoli|Napoli]], [[Palermo F.C.|Palermo]], and [[Reggina 1914|Reggina]].

The new match ball was the [[Nike Inc.|Nike]] T90 Omni.

On 16 May 2009, [[Inter Milan|Internazionale]] won the league by holding an unassailable lead after [[A.C. Milan]]'s loss away to [[Udinese Calcio|Udinese]].

==Rule changes==
The 2008–09 season saw new rules relating to the transfer of player registration introduced. Clubs without non-[[European Union|EU]] players in their squad were allowed three incoming non-EU player transfers (whereas previously only newly promoted clubs could have three). Clubs with one non-EU player were allowed two such transfers and clubs with two non-EU players were permitted one transfer and a further one if they cancelled the registration of one of their non-EU players or that player gained EU nationality. Clubs with three or more non-EU players were given two conditional quotas with the caveat that the release (as opposed to transfer) of two non-EU players as free agent would only allow for one further non-EU signing.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.figc.it/Assets/contentresources_2/ContenutoGenerico/45.$plit/C_2_ContenutoGenerico_19186_StrilloComunicatoUfficiale_lstAllegati_Allegato_0_upfAllegato.pdf|title=Comunicato n° 003/A del 3 luglio 2008/|date=3 July 2008|access-date=1 February 2010|publisher=FIGC|language=it|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120323015900/http://www.figc.it/Assets/contentresources_2/ContenutoGenerico/45.$plit/C_2_ContenutoGenerico_19186_StrilloComunicatoUfficiale_lstAllegati_Allegato_0_upfAllegato.pdf|archive-date=23 March 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref>
==Teams==
Three teams were promoted from [[2007–08 Serie B|Serie B]]: [[A.C. ChievoVerona|Chievo]], [[Bologna F.C. 1909|Bologna]], and [[U.S. Lecce|Lecce]]. The first two earned direct promotion, while Lecce won the promotional playoffs, defeating [[U.C. AlbinoLeffe|AlbinoLeffe]] 2–1 on aggregate in a two-legged playoff final.
